gaps.target_position: Service-model position (Tension 5): the DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS Environment block on lingered hosts is justified by notification delivery, and the roadmap's notify.mqtt item assumes org.freedesktop.Notifications works once the session bus is reachable from the User=io system service.

org.freedesktop.Notifications D-Bus activation without desktop environment lingered systemd user session
cage wayland kiosk single client notification daemon second process WAYLAND_DISPLAY
gaps.rationale: Directly audited (per run directives): grep for mako|dunst|swaync|fnott|announcr across /home/io/projects/jupiter-os returns ZERO matches — no notification daemon ships anywhere in the fleet, so org.freedesktop.Notifications delivery is dead code on every host TODAY, not merely 'untested from a system service' as comparisons.md frames it. The service-model investigator's own open question #1 anticipated exactly this. What no corpus source answers: (a) whether ANY notification daemon can render under cage — a single-client kiosk compositor where the daemon must share the session's Wayland socket as a second user-session process; (b) whether org.freedesktop.Notifications can be D-Bus-activated from a lingered user manager with no graphical session manager parenting it. If no daemon is viable under cage, the session-bus Environment block loses its last justification entirely (notifications must route to the customer-display VFD's MQTT overlay instead, which IS verified live per customer-display.nix's header), which would simplify the system-service design and change the roadmap's notify item's last-mile from 'session bus' to 'MQTT-to-VFD'. The draft must not present the Environment block as load-bearing without this source.

This is the most load-bearing UNVERIFIED feature claim in the committed positions.

gaps.rationale: This is the investigator's own flip condition #2, and nothing in the corpus searches for its expiry. The evidence chain is Feb 2023 (tejing's Discourse) + one Oct 2025 Discourse note; NixOS moves fast (the fleet pins nixos-unstable — verified in jupiter-os/flake.nix), and there is active upstream work on user-manager reactivation (user-unit reload-on-switch has recurring nixpkgs PRs). If ANY change post-Oct-2025 made nixos-rebuild switch reactivate lingered users' units, Position A's simplicity becomes competitive again and the draft's central 'retire the user-unit shape entirely' commitment weakens to a preference — a structural rewrite of the fleet-service-model chapter. If the gap is confirmed still-open as of 2026, the draft can commit harder and cite the current thread rather than a stale one. Either way the draft currently cites a 4-month-old snapshot for its single most load-bearing lifecycle fact; the fetch is cheap and decisive.

gaps.target_position: Testing-gate position (Tension 4): step 5 of the 7-step ladder — a mosquitto-subprocess harness (bind 127.0.0.1:0, spawn mosquitto, TCP-probe readiness) inside craneLib.cargoTest, because 'nix flake check on remote NixOS builders IS the CI'.
search_queries: nix build sandbox loopback network 127.0.0.1 tests bind connect
nix flake check cargo test integration test socket network namespace sandbox
nix sandbox ip link set lo up build isolation localhost
gaps.rationale: The testing-gate report eliminated testcontainers on ground truth (no container runtime — I re-verified: no docker/podman in jupiter-os hosts or modules, /etc/nix/machines lists 5 remote NixOS builders) but NEVER addressed whether the Nix BUILD sandbox itself permits the substitute harness: binding a loopback TCP socket, spawning a daemon subprocess, and connecting to it. The report's own zbus section acknowledges 'a Nix build sandbox has no session bus and no /run' — the same sandbox properties may bite the mosquitto harness (loopback interface state in the build network namespace is a known Nix gotcha; I could not probe locally — unshare is not permitted on this host). If sandbox networking blocks the harness, step 5 must move entirely into the runNixOSTest VM (restructuring the ladder's cost and the 'crane gives the binary to tests for free' claim) or escape the sandbox with __noChroot (undermining the hermetic-CI story). One authoritative source — Nix manual sandbox semantics or a nixpkgs issue/test showing loopback TCP client-server tests in-sandbox — either confirms the design as-written or forces the restructure before the draft bakes it in.

gaps.target_position: Service-model position: 'retire the user-unit shape entirely' + 'niri and Plasma appear in zero host configs' — the per-session environment (NIRI_SOCKET, WAYLAND_DISPLAY) is dismissed as a current non-requirement.

gaps.rationale: The investigator's flip condition #3 has a scheduled trigger, not just a hypothetical one: europa's own configuration comment says 'the future dev workstation (himalia) opts in' (to the dev-tool modules it disables), and the agent already ships a backend-niri gated on NIRI_SOCKET in io's session environment (verified: backend-niri/src/lib.rs:24). The corpus documents that niri's IPC is a UNIX socket at $NIRI_SOCKET (ipc-niri-msg-niri note) but never establishes WHERE that socket lives or how a process OUTSIDE the session could reach it — the exact question a User=io system service on a future himalia-class desktop host must answer. If niri's socket is only reachable via session-scoped env/paths (it is created under the session's runtime), the system-service-everywhere design needs a per-session bridge (or a host-class carve-out) the current spec lacks. The draft's 'retire the user-unit shape entirely' should be conditioned on this source — otherwise the roadmap's module design (role-driven mkIf) omits the one host class jupiterOS has already announced.

gaps.target_position: MQTT-lifecycle position (Tension 2/agent.rs audit D9): callisto mosquitto needs max_queued_messages ≥ 4× fleet retained inventory (recommended 8192) because the default 1000 is 'empirically the silent retained-drop mechanism from HA #135266', plus persistence true.
search_queries: mosquitto $SYS broker statistics messages dropped queue metrics
mosquitto max_queued_messages default 1000 home assistant restart retained replay threshold
home assistant mqtt integration subscribes all retained messages restart queue overflow per client
gaps.rationale: This is the MQTT investigator's own flip condition #4, and I can now half-test it with a live measurement the draft should inherit correctly calibrated: the connected HA instance on callisto carries only ~22-25 agent-created entities (measured via HA template: 15 agent sensor entities + 7 control entities across the 4 agent hosts, on a 1267-state instance), so the spec's own sizing rule gives 4×R ≈ ~140 — an order of magnitude BELOW the default 1000 and two below the recommended 8192. The sizing claim extrapolates from a single 5374-entity incident; at jupiterOS's actual scale the mechanism may never bind — UNLESS the binding quantity is the broker-WIDE retained replay HA receives on its broad subscription at restart (the number that actually overflowed in #135266), which is unknown for this broker. Needed: (a) independent confirmation of the silent-drop mechanism (mosquitto $SYS drop counters / docs beyond the single HA issue — currently one-source per redundancy analysis); (b) evidence pinning WHICH count overflows the per-client queue (agent entity inventory vs broker-wide retained). The draft's D9 fix should land as either 'urgent sizing, empirically triggered at this scale' or 'cheap hygiene + a $SYS confirmation check' — the difference is exactly the calibration that separates a credible reliability roadmap from an over-prescriptive one. (The persistence-true claim is independently solid per mosquitto.conf(5) and stands regardless.)
